options.option_text: Taciturn (antonym — taciturn = reserved, saying very little)
Loquacious (correct: garrulous = excessively talkative; loquacious = talkative, fond of talking ✓)
Reticent (antonym — reticent = not readily revealing thoughts or feelings)
Laconic (antonym — laconic = using very few words)

questions.explanation: B is correct. GARRULOUS = excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters. Synonym = LOQUACIOUS, VOLUBLE, VERBOSE, CHATTY. All wrong options are antonyms. Memory: garrulous comes from Latin garrire (to chatter).

options.option_text: Aggravate (antonym — aggravate = make worse)
Improve (correct: ameliorate = make something bad better; improve ✓)
Deteriorate (antonym — deteriorate = become worse over time)
Exacerbate (antonym — exacerbate = make worse; intensify)

questions.explanation: B is correct. AMELIORATE = to make something bad better. Synonym = IMPROVE, ALLEVIATE, MITIGATE, RECTIFY. All wrong options mean 'to worsen.' 'The new policy ameliorated the working conditions.'

options.option_text: Pessimistic (antonym — pessimistic = tending to expect the worst outcomes)
Optimistic (correct: sanguine = optimistic, especially in difficult situations ✓)
Despondent (antonym — despondent = in low spirits from loss of hope)
Gloomy (antonym — gloomy = dark, pessimistic, dispirited)

questions.explanation: B is correct. SANGUINE = optimistic, confident. From Latin sanguis (blood) — a 'sanguine temperament' was cheerful in medieval humour theory. Synonym = OPTIMISTIC, HOPEFUL, UPBEAT, BUOYANT. Antonyms: pessimistic, gloomy, despondent, melancholic.

options.option_text: Generous (antonym — generous = willing to give more than expected)
Miserly (correct: parsimonious = very unwilling to spend money; miserly ✓)
Munificent (antonym — munificent = more generous than usual)
Lavish (antonym — lavish = sumptuously generous)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PARSIMONIOUS = very unwilling to spend money or use resources. Synonym = MISERLY, NIGGARDLY, STINGY, TIGHT-FISTED, PENURIOUS. Antonyms: generous, lavish, munificent, extravagant.

options.option_text: Occasional (antonym — occasional = happening from time to time)
Habitual (correct: inveterate = deeply established habit unlikely to change; habitual ✓)
Temporary (antonym — temporary = lasting only for a short time)
Sporadic (antonym — sporadic = occurring at irregular intervals)

questions.explanation: B is correct. INVETERATE = having a habit deeply established that is unlikely to change. Synonym = HABITUAL, CONFIRMED, CHRONIC, DEEP-ROOTED, INCORRIGIBLE. 'An inveterate liar' = habitual liar. Antonyms: occasional, temporary, sporadic, intermittent.

options.option_text: Reckless (antonym — reckless = heedless of danger or consequences)
Prudent (correct: judicious = showing good judgment; prudent = acting with care and forethought ✓)
Impulsive (antonym — impulsive = acting without careful consideration)
Foolhardy (antonym — foolhardy = recklessly bold without thought for danger)

questions.explanation: B is correct. JUDICIOUS = having or showing good judgment or sense. Synonym = PRUDENT, WISE, SAGACIOUS, SENSIBLE, DISCERNING. 'A judicious use of resources.' Note: judicial = relating to courts; judicious = showing wisdom. Common confusable pair.

options.option_text: Salutary (antonym — salutary = producing good/beneficial effects)
Deleterious (correct: pernicious = causing harm or ruin; deleterious = causing harm or damage ✓)
Wholesome (antonym — wholesome = conducive to good health)
Beneficial (antonym — beneficial = advantageous, helpful)

questions.explanation: B is correct. PERNICIOUS = causing insidious harm or ruin. Synonym = DELETERIOUS, HARMFUL, NOXIOUS, INJURIOUS, DETRIMENTAL. 'Smoking has pernicious effects on health.' Antonyms: salutary, beneficial, wholesome, benign.

options.option_text: Affluent (antonym — affluent = having abundant money)
Indigent (correct: impecunious = having little or no money; indigent = poor, needy ✓)
Opulent (antonym — opulent = ostentatiously rich)
Prosperous (antonym — prosperous = successful, especially financially)

questions.explanation: B is correct. IMPECUNIOUS = having little or no money. From Latin pecunia (money). Synonym = INDIGENT, DESTITUTE, PENNILESS, INSOLVENT, PENURIOUS. Antonyms: affluent, opulent, prosperous, wealthy.

options.option_text: Docile (antonym — docile = submissive, easily managed)
Intractable (correct: recalcitrant = stubbornly uncooperative; intractable = hard to control ✓)
Amenable (antonym — amenable = willing to cooperate or yield)
Compliant (antonym — compliant = willing to obey rules)

questions.explanation: B is correct. RECALCITRANT = stubbornly uncooperative toward authority. Synonym = INTRACTABLE, OBSTINATE, REFRACTORY, DEFIANT, UNRULY. 'The recalcitrant child refused to follow instructions.' Antonyms: docile, amenable, compliant, tractable.

options.option_text: Voluble (antonym — voluble = talking fluently and at length)
Laconic (correct: taciturn = reserved, uncommunicative; laconic = using very few words ✓)
Garrulous (antonym — garrulous = excessively talkative)
Verbose (antonym — verbose = using more words than needed)

questions.explanation: B is correct. TACITURN = reserved, not inclined to talk. Synonym = LACONIC, RETICENT, RESERVED, TERSE, MONOSYLLABIC. Antonyms: voluble, garrulous, verbose, loquacious — all meaning talkative. 'His taciturn manner made him seem cold and unfriendly.'
